statement: Kawasaki says the VIN on its motorcycles is stamped on the steering head, below the handlebars. On a used KX, read it there yourself and compare it, character by character, with the title or bill of sale; Kawasaki US VINs begin JKA or JKB.

vals.vin_location: stamped on the steering head, below the handlebars
vals.wmi: JKA or JKB (seen in Kawasaki's own US VIN filings and recall VIN ranges)

notes: General Kawasaki motorcycle statement, not a KX-specific manual page. The engine-number location was not confirmed from a Kawasaki document in this pass. JKA/JKB prefixes appear in Kawasaki's 2019 VIN filings (on-road models, https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/mid/home/displayfile/39cbd4aa-de4b-4320-b68a-6994c6512ec7) and in the 2025 KX450 recall VIN ranges in kawasaki.json.

source.name: Kawasaki parts site, how to identify your vehicle (VIN finder)

topic: Yamaha YZ: VIN on the steering head, model label on both sides
statement: The US regulator's notice for the 2022 YZ125 says the VIN is stamped on the frame steering head and the model number is printed on both sides of the bike. Yamaha's own older YZ450F owner's service manual (2016) puts the VIN on the right side of the frame and the engine serial number on the raised part of the right side of the engine.

vals.vin_location: stamped on the frame steering head
vals.model_label: printed on both the right and left sides
vals.engine_number_2016_yz450f: stamped into the elevated part of the right side of the engine

notes: Recorded against the only roster bike the notice names. The 2016 YZ450F manual page (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1161595/Yamaha-Yz450f.html?page=19) is outside the roster years and is given for the engine number only. The notice quotes the VIN range as ***CE34C***000301-004096, so recall notices may quote only part of a VIN. The recall itself is ki6-013.

source.name: CPSC recall notice 22-746 (Yamaha Motor Corporation USA), 2022 YZ125

topic: used RM-Z450: missed shifts and false neutrals
statement: Owners of 2014-on RM-Z450s, including the 2018-on generation, report missed shifts and false neutrals, most often 2nd to 3rd under hard acceleration; several blame the short stock shift lever and fix it with a longer one, and one bike needed gears and shift forks replaced. On a used RM-Z450, shift through every gear under load on the test ride and ask whether the gearbox has been opened.

vals.test_ride: hard upshifts 2-3 and 3-4 under load; downshifts; note any neutral between gears
vals.owner_fixes: longer or aftermarket shift lever (most common); stiffer shift-drum follower spring kit; one case needed 2nd-5th gears and shift forks

notes: In the 2019 thread (all posts 2019-04-10) two posters report shifting trouble: a friend's 2018 hit false neutrals and was having its transmission rebuilt at 44 hours, and another says a different shift lever helps a lot; a third suggests a longer lever. A 2017 thread on 2014-2016 bikes agrees (https://vitalmx.com/forums/Tech-Help-Race-Shop,42/14-and-newer-RMZ450-shifting,1314043, Feb-Mar 2017): about three owners report false neutrals, mostly 2nd to 3rd under hard acceleration, four recommend a longer lever, and one owner's 2015 had 2nd-5th gears and the shift forks replaced at about 5 hours; one says his 2017 is much better. Four owners in the 2019 thread report no problems at all. No report read for 2020-2025 bikes specifically; applied to them because the 2018-on engine and gearbox carr

source.name: Vital MX forum thread on 2018 RM-Z450 faults

topic: Honda CRF: where the VIN and engine number are
statement: Honda's 2020 owner's manuals put the VIN on the right side of the steering head on both the CRF250R/RX and the CRF450R/RX, but the engine number on different sides: the left crankcase on the CRF250R/RX and the right crankcase on the CRF450R/RX. On a used CRF, read both numbers off the bike and match them to the paperwork; US Honda VINs begin JH2.

vals.vin_location: stamped on the right side of the steering head
vals.wmi: JH2 (Honda Motor Co., motorcycle; NHTSA vPIC)

notes: CRF450R side from Honda's 2020 CRF450R/RX/RWE owner's manual 31MKE630 (https://2rom-prd-data.hondamotopub.com/om/AHM/CRF450RX-R-RWE/2020/CRF450R.RX.RWE_31MKE630_0.pdf, page 172, dated 2019-04-03), already held as p6h-017. This settles the earlier conflict: the left-crankcase reading in an older CRF450R edition matches the CRF250R layout, so the side depends on the model and possibly the generation. Honda's 2025 European CRF250R manual shows the frame and engine numbers only in a drawing. WMI from https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeWMI/JH2?format=json. Read 2026-11-07.

source.name: Honda 2020 CRF250R/RX owner's manual 31K95620, vehicle identification page

topic: Suzuki RM-Z: where the frame and engine numbers are
statement: Suzuki's RM-Z450 owner's service manual (2008 edition) says the frame number is stamped on the steering head and the engine serial number on the right side of the crankcase. Later RM-Z owner's service manuals keep a serial number location page; check the one for the bike's year. US Suzuki VINs begin JS1.

vals.vin_location: stamped on the steering head (2008 RM-Z450 manual)
vals.engine_number: stamped on the right side of the crankcase (2008 RM-Z450 manual)
vals.wmi: JS1 (Suzuki Motor Corporation, motorcycle; NHTSA vPIC)

notes: The only Suzuki document whose serial-number page could be read in this pass is for the 2008 RM-Z450, twelve or more years before these bikes; a 2021 RM-Z250 owner's manual listing shows a SERIAL NUMBER LOCATION heading but its text was not readable, and one manual site sits behind a bot check, which was not worked around. Applied with low confidence: steering-head frame numbers are the norm, but the crankcase side is not confirmed for current bikes. WMI from https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeWMI/JS1?format=json. Read 2026-11-07.

source.name: Suzuki RM-Z450 (K8) owner's service manual, serial number location

topic: KTM-group VIN: what each position means (US filing)
statement: KTM North America's VIN filing with the US regulator (September 2025) gives one world manufacturer code, VBK, for KTM AG, with Husqvarna and GasGas shown as brand prefixes in the model code. Positions 4-5 are the model code (competition codes such as SX, MX, XC, XW), 6 a power class, 7 the engine type (2 two-stroke, 4 four-stroke, 0 electric), 8 the usage type (3 = closed-course competition), 9 the check digit, 10 the model year, 11 the plant (M = Mattighofen, Austria), 12 an engine-capacity digit, and 13-17 the serial.

vals.positions: 1-3 WMI; 4-5 model code; 6 net power class; 7 engine type 2/4/0; 8 usage 0/3/E; 9 check digit; 10 model year; 11 plant (M = Mattighofen); 12 engine capacity; 13-17 serial
vals.brand_prefixes: HQV Husqvarna, GG GasGas, HSB Husaberg (in the model code)
vals.used_buyer_check: A KTM, Husqvarna or GasGas competition bike's VIN should start VBK, carry the year letter in position 10 and, per this filing, a 2 or 4 in position 7 that matches the engine.

notes: Applied to 2026-2027 only because the filing is dated September 2025; earlier years very likely use the same scheme (CPSC recall notices for 2022-2025 KTM-group bikes quote the 10th character as the year) but the earlier filings were not read. The filing does not list the model-year letters itself; those come from 49 CFR 565.15 (L 2020 ... V 2027). Read 2026-11-07.

source.name: KTM North America Inc. VIN information submitted under 49 CFR 565 (NHTSA vPIC manufacturer file)

topic: electronic proof of service in the 2025 service schedules
statement: The 2025 KTM, Husqvarna and GasGas owner's manual service schedules include a line to enter an electronic proof of service (KTM's wording: in the dealer portal) once after the first operating hour and at the 15, 45 and 90-hour services and every 24 months. When buying used, ask whether a dealer did those services: a dealer-serviced bike may have a digital service record a dealer can confirm.

vals.schedule_line: Enter electronic proof of service (KTM: in the dealer portal)
vals.when: once after 1 operating hour; every 15, 45 and 90 operating hours; every 24 months

notes: Schedule line read from the extracted 2025 manual tables kept in docs/research/expansion/gaps/ktm-torques (same CDN as the other KTM-group manuals in this repo). The manuals do not say who can see the record or whether a dealer can look it up by VIN for a buyer: that part is BAK's inference, stated as may. Not checked in pre-2025 manuals; 2026 manuals in a separate record.

source.name: KTM 2025 450 SX-F / 450 XC-F owner's manual 25_3240045_en_OM, service schedule

topic: electronic proof of service in the 2026 service schedules
statement: The 2026 owner's manual service schedules for these KTM, Husqvarna and GasGas models also include entering an electronic proof of service once after the first operating hour, at the 15, 45 and 90-hour services and every 24 months, so a buyer can ask whether the bike was dealer-serviced and has that record.

vals.when: once after one operating hour; every 15, 45 and 90 operating hours; every 24 months

notes: Only the 2026 documents whose extracted tables show the line are listed; the line was not seen in the extracts for other 2026 models, which may mean the extract missed it rather than that the manual lacks it.

source.name: KTM 2026 125 SX / 125 XC owner's manual 26_3240232_en_BA, service schedule

topic: used Husqvarna: composite subframe cracks and seam gaps
statement: Many Husqvarna owners report that the composite (plastic) subframe cracks after crashes, tip-overs or hard off-road use, and some report breaks without a crash; earlier owners also found the airbox seams separating, letting dirt past the filter. On a used Husqvarna, pull the seat and side panels, look for cracks around the mounting points and along the seams, and shine a light from the fender side into the airbox to spot gaps.

vals.check: seat and side panels off; cracks at mounts and seams; light test into the airbox; dirt on the clean side of the filter
vals.fix: replacement composite subframe (a parts listing quoted in an owner thread, Nov 2020 - Feb 2021: about $210 plus shipping); sealant on seam gaps
vals.years_reported: seam gaps 2013-2016; cracks reported on 2017, 2019 TE 250i, 2020 FC 450, 2020 250F and 2020 TE 300

notes: About ten posters in the first thread (posts 2017-01-25/26 and 2020-09-13/14; several second-hand), including breaks after crashes and without one, agreeing with two owner-forum threads: https://www.cafehusky.com/threads/cracked-my-subframe-do-they-sell-aluminum-ones.91277 (2019 TE 250i, Nov 2020 - Feb 2021) and https://www.cafehusky.com/threads/my-subframe-is-coming-apart-better-check-yours.81998/page-2 (seam gaps 2013-2016, Oct 2015 - Sep 2017). A dealer in the first thread reported no subframe problems among ordinary customers, so this is mostly crash and hard-use damage. The 2022 FC 350/450 crack is already kg7-097 and is not repeated; the 2022 models below are in used-hq-002. 2023+ bikes not covered by these reports.

source.name: Vital MX forum thread on Husqvarna subframes (2017 and 2020 posts)

statement: Owners of this Husqvarna generation report composite subframe cracks after crashes and hard off-road use, and sometimes without a crash. On a used bike, take the seat and side panels off and look for cracks at the mounts and along the seams, and check the clean side of the air filter for dirt that got past a gap.

vals.check: seat and side panels off; cracks at mounts and seams; dirt on the clean side of the filter

notes: Extends the 2016-2021 owner reports (used-hq-001) to the 2022 carry-over models; the agreeing owner-forum report is https://www.cafehusky.com/threads/cracked-my-subframe-do-they-sell-aluminum-ones.91277 (2019 TE 250i). No 2022-specific report was read for these models. FC 350/450 2022 are covered by kg7-097.
